messages.content: use unless in a sentence about going for a walk if there is no rain.
we will go for a walk unless there is rain.
now only give the part that could stop the walk.
unless there is rain.
what does that mean in simple words?
we plan to walk. if there is rain, that may change the plan.
does it mean we are sure to stay home if there is rain?
not from those words alone. rain is the thing that may stop the plan, but you have not said what you will do instead.
make that explanation shorter.
rain may change the walk plan, but you have not said what you will do instead.
now make it sure we stay home if there is rain.
we will go for a walk unless there is rain. if there is rain, we will stay home.
can i use if there is no rain instead?
yes. we will go for a walk if there is no rain gives the same idea for when the walk can happen.
give that sentence without another explanation.
we will go for a walk if there is no rain.
write a story about a child looking at a clock and still not knowing whether a shop is open. the detail he needs should be the day.

a child looked at the clock and saw that it was four. he remembered his mother saying that the shop closed at five. he asked whether they could walk there now. she said that closing time was for some days, but the shop was closed all day today. he had remembered a time without keeping in mind which days it was for. they looked at the shop message together and chose another day. before leaving next time, he asked about both the day and the hours. the clock still helped, but it was only one part of the information they needed.
what did he know at first?
he knew the clock time was four and remembered a closing time of five.
what did he not know?
he did not know that the shop was closed on that day.
why was four before five not enough?
because the shop was not open at all that day. that day did not use the hours he remembered.
only give the reason about today.
the shop was closed all day today.
what could he ask before going next time?
is the shop open today, and what time does it close?
finish with a visit on a day when it is open.
on the new day, they checked the hours before walking there. the child looked at the clock and told his mother they had time.
my friend said i need a quiet evening. i want to reply without making it sound like i need the quiet evening myself.
you could say: i understand you need a quiet evening. we can talk another time.
what if i only write i need a quiet evening back to them?
that would usually sound like you are talking about yourself. if you are talking about their need, use you or say that those are the words they sent.
make that explanation shorter.
use you for their need. i would usually mean your own need in your reply.
can you make the reply shorter?
i understand. we can talk another time.
i have not said i want another talk yet. keep it only about understanding.
i understand that you need a quiet evening.
can i add take care?
yes. i understand that you need a quiet evening. take care.
why did you not say i know why?
you have said they need quiet, not that you know every reason. understanding the request is different from knowing the whole story.
only give the short reply with take care.
i understand. take care.
i have five containers. three are full and two are empty. i make one empty container full of food. how many are full now?
four are full, and one is empty.
what if i only put some food into it, without making it full?
then three are full for sure. the container you changed has some food, and one is still empty.
that is useful. i only put a little food in. how many are still empty?
one is still empty. the other one now has food, even if it is not full.
how many containers have food?
four, if the three full containers all have food too.
yes, all had food. how many containers are there in all?
there are still five containers.
only give that number.
five.
why did the number not change?
you changed what was inside one container. you did not add or take away a container.
only give how many are full for sure.
three are full for sure.
i enjoyed a story, but i did not understand the last part. can both be true?
yes. you can enjoy a story without every part being clear to you.
i liked the people and the way they talked. i just do not know why one person left at the end.
you have a specific question about that choice. you can talk about what you liked and still ask about the part you did not understand.
help me ask a friend who read the same story.
i liked the people in the story, but i did not understand why that person left at the end. what did you think was the reason?
can you answer the reason yourself?
not without the story or more details. i need more of the story before i can answer that question.
make that explanation shorter.
i need more details from the story first.
what if i want a made up reason for a new story instead?
then we can choose a reason for a new story and keep clear that it is made up.
just give my question to the friend again.
i liked the people in the story, but i did not understand why that person left at the end. what did you think was the reason?
write a story about someone asking which book is best and getting a better answer after saying what they want to learn.

a woman came to the library and asked a worker which book was best. the worker looked at the shelf and asked what she wanted from the book. she said she wanted to learn how plants grow, using simple words and pictures. now the worker could show her a book with a short explanation on each page and clear pictures. another book on the same shelf had more detail, but it was not the best start for her question. she chose the simple one and asked whether she could come back for the longer book later. giving her goal had helped turn best from a general word into a choice for what she needed now.
why was best not enough by itself?
it did not say what the book needed to do for her. different books can help people who want different things.
what details helped the worker choose?
she wanted to learn about growing plants with simple words and pictures.
did choosing the simple book say she could never read the longer one?
no. it was a starting choice for now, not a rule for every later day.
write her request after she gives the goal.
which book would help me start learning about how plants grow? i would like simple words and pictures.
finish with her choosing a page to read first.
she opened the book and looked at the first picture. then she sat down to read the words next to it.
what could she do if one part was still hard?
she could ask about that specific part instead of choosing to call the whole book wrong for her.
my sister and i share a book. when i tell someone about it, can i say our book?
yes. our book can be the book that you and your sister share.
what if someone else is talking to a friend about the same book?
they could say their book when talking about you and your sister.
does the book itself change when our is changed to their?
no. the words change with who is talking. the book and the people who share it can stay the same.
make that explanation shorter.
it can be the same book. the word changes with who is talking.
that sentence is hard. say it more simply.
you call it our book. another person can call it their book when talking about you and your sister.
now make it a book that only my sister has as her own.
you can say her book. your sister can say my book.
why does my not always mean me in every message?
my goes with the person saying the words. when your sister says my book, she is talking about her book.
make that answer shorter.
my is about the person saying the sentence.
that answers my question. please do not ask me another one now.
okay. i will leave it there.
can you give me a kind last sentence without telling me what to do?
i hope the answer is useful for you.
now make it shorter.
i hope it helps.
can you say goodbye without saying what time of day it is?
goodbye, and take care.
why not good night?
you asked me not to choose a time of day. goodbye works without that detail.
only goodbye now.
goodbye.
